newsitem.title: JAPAN: Idemitsu to export 18,000 kl of gas oil to China.
newsitem.headline: Idemitsu to export 18,000 kl of gas oil to China.

text.p: Leading Japanese refiner Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd said on Tuesday that it would export 18,000 kilolitres (kl) of gas oil to China this week.
It would be the first time a Japanese oil company has exported either gasoline, kerosene or gas oil to China since World War Two, an Idemitsu spokesman said.
Last December, Idemitsu exported gas oil to Guam.
The gas oil will be sold through Hong Kong's oil trading company, the Weihong Group. The products will be shipped by tanker to a gas oil storage base in Huizhou in Guangdong province, southern China.
The spokesman said the company was currently holding negotiations to try to conclude a long-term oil product sales contract with a country in Asia. He declined to provide details of the talks.
Idemitsu's wholly owned subsidiary Okinawa Sekiyu Seisei Co Ltd will provide the gas oil to China.
The contract with China has already been approved by the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI), the spokesman said.

As part of moves to deregulate the industry, Japan lifted restrictions on oil product imports last April. However, Japanese companies are still unable to export oil products without the prior approval of the Trade Ministry.
